method: Reviewed the full interrupt/resume lesson, its registered source checkpoints, SQL sketch, runnable Python fixture, numeric and historical claims, failure boundaries, and adjacent conclusions. Added a crash-window fixture where the receiver has committed but the caller crashes before persisting its receipt, then used test-first verification to expose that stale local approved state incorrectly returned expired instead of reconciling. Updated the fixture to reconcile a matching authoritative receiver record before expiry handling. Executed the one Python fence and compared it with the preserved prior verifier. No provider or external-service calls were made.

observations.trace: The local deterministic model now reconciles a matching receiver ledger record even when local state remains approved after a crash and the approval claim deadline has passed; it does not resend. It separately rejects a delayed first claim after expiry and reconciles an unknown/lost receipt. The lesson states that lookup absence is not proof unless the receiver offers an authoritative idempotency contract. The W6 verifier passes 34/34, and the preserved 2026-10-21 verifier passes 28/28.

limitations: The in-memory fixture is sequential and models authoritative receiver evidence; it does not test a real process crash, database persistence, concurrent workers, or a production receiver API.
No real identity provider, authorization policy, queue, outbox, or external side effect was exercised.
Historical Chapter 11 injection and provider observations were not replayed because raw traces and scoring artifacts are unavailable.
